description: Adam: gradient descent with a memory, a running mean of the gradient and of its square, so every step has about the same size whatever the gradient's scale.

line_docs: Name the parameters as one tuple Θ: the pair of W and B.
The gradient of the loss with respect to the whole tuple: a pair, one entry per parameter.
One step of the optimizer state: the pair (M V) is updated on G by the placeholder glyph ↻; the paper's two moment lines, and both parameters, in one.
The corrected first moment: M divided by 1 − β₁ to the power T.
The corrected second moment: V divided by 1 − β₂ to the power T.
The step for the whole tuple at once: Θ moves by η times M̂ over √V̂ + ε, both parameters in one line.
m.purpose: Θ names the parameter pair (W B); G is its gradient pair; the placeholder ↻ steps the state pair (M V) on G in one line, where the paper needs two; the corrected moments and the step are written once and hold for both parameters. This is the research's case for tuples: Adam's state is parameters, two moments and a step count, and the notation should carry it as one value. Placeholder glyphs.
m.text:
Θ ← (W B)
G ← ∇Θ L
(M V) ← ↻ (M V) G
M̂ ← M ÷ 1−β₁*T
V̂ ← V ÷ 1−β₂*T
Θ ← Θ − η×M̂ ÷ √V̂ + ε
m.title: The same update over tuples: the state travels as one thing

line_docs: The gradient of the loss with respect to the weight, at the current parameters; b has one of its own.
The first moment: keep β₁ of the old running mean, add 1 − β₁ of the new gradient.
The second moment: the same running mean, of the squared gradient.
The corrections: both moments start at zero, so for the first steps they are divided by 1 − βᵗ to undo the bias toward zero.
The step: move w by η times the corrected mean over the root of the corrected square, plus ε; a step of about η whatever the gradient's scale.
The same step for b, with b's own gradient, moments and corrections: on paper the rules are repeated per parameter.
math.purpose: Six lines: the gradient; the first moment, a running mean of the gradient; the second, a running mean of its square; the two corrected for starting at zero; and the step, the corrected mean divided by the root of the corrected square. The last line repeats the step for b: on paper every parameter gets its own copy of the rules and its own m and v.
math.title: The update as the paper writes it, one scalar at a time

name: adam

docs: The gradient of the one-neuron loss at the current parameters, from sw-MLPL's grad: one number for w, one for b.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
How much the loss changes for a small change in one parameter.
The one-neuron loss, the mean squared error of ŷ = wx + b over the first stone's four points; the same loss and the same start as the first stone, so the two paths compare.
The neuron's slope. Adam moves it by about η per step whatever the gradient's size.
A running mean of the gradient: mostly the old mean, a little of the new gradient. It smooths the direction. Starts at zero.
Assignment: the new value replaces the old.
β₁, how much of the old mean is kept each step; here 0.9, so the mean remembers about ten gradients.
Multiply: by juxtaposition on paper, × in the notation.
Add.
Open parenthesis.
One.
Subtract.
Close parenthesis.
A running mean of the squared gradient: how big the gradient has been lately, direction ignored. Starts at zero.
β₂, how much of the old squared mean is kept; here 0.999, a long memory, so the scale settles slowly.
Square the gradient: its size, direction ignored.
m divided by 1 − β₁ᵗ: the running mean starts at zero and is too small for the first steps; the correction undoes that.
Divide.
Which step this is, counting from one; the stone's time axis. The corrections shrink to nothing as t grows.
Separates the two corrections.
v divided by 1 − β₂ᵗ, the same correction for the second moment.
η, about how far each step goes; here 0.1, the first stone's rate, so the two paths compare.
The root of the corrected second moment: the gradient's typical size, in the gradient's own units.
ε, a tiny number (10⁻⁸) that keeps the division safe when the second moment is zero.
The neuron's intercept, updated by the same rules with its own gradient and moments.
Θ, the pair (W B): the notation names the parameters once and every line below moves both. Adam's whole state, the parameters, the two moments and the step count, is a tuple like this.
∇Θ L, the gradient of the loss with respect to the parameter tuple, a pair.

↻, the research's placeholder for one step of the optimizer state: the pair (M V) goes in with the gradient pair, the pair comes out with both moments updated. One glyph where the paper writes two lines.
β raised to the step count, *T in the notation (APL's power).

title: Adam

visual.purpose: The dataflow of one step with the state looping through ↻; the four moments as bars, a pair each for w and b; and the parameter plane with two paths from the same start on the same loss: Adam's, and plain gradient descent's from the first stone, replayed from its own trace.
visual.title: The state as bars, and two paths through parameter space
